rules.shopNote: VAT 20% is included in the price (the 10% rate applies to restaurants and hotels). Visitors can claim VAT back on goods bought for 2,000 dirhams or more at one seller on the same day (food excluded).

rules.name: Egypt

taxes.name: VAT
taxes.basis: 14% for licensed tourist restaurants and for other restaurants above the registration threshold; reports disagree on whether menus show it

serviceCharge.note: About 12% service is added in tourist establishments (Lonely Planet says 10%).

tip.note: A service charge is usually added, so leave a little extra in cash for the waiter; about 10% if there is none.

rules.note: A 2020 chamber statement says tourist-establishment menus must show all-inclusive prices, but a 2023 report says diners pay 26% (12% service, 14% VAT) on top. Assume tax and service are added until the menu says otherwise.

sources.title: Egyptian Tax Authority: restaurants and cafes subject to VAT per Finance Minister decisions (18 May 2025; Arabic)
sources.covers: Restaurants licensed by the Ministry of Tourism are subject to VAT at the general rate of 14%; non-tourist restaurants are taxed at 14% once they reach the registration threshold under Law 67 of 2016.

sources.title: Tourist establishments oblige restaurants to announce prices inclusive of taxes and service - Youm7 (14 Aug 2020; Arabic)
sources.covers: Headline: the tourist-establishments chamber requires restaurants to announce prices including taxes and service.

sources.title: Albawaba News (26 Aug 2020; Arabic)
sources.covers: Menu prices used to leave out the roughly 12% service fee and the 14% VAT; after adding them prices looked slightly higher.

sources.title: Tourist establishments: restaurants add 26% service and tax on meals - Shorouk News (17 Jul 2023; Arabic headline)
sources.covers: Headline puts the extra charge at 26% (service and tax) on top of meal prices, in conflict with the 2020 chamber statement.

sources.title: The Ultimate Guide to Tipping in Africa (Lonely Planet, 27 Sep 2024)
sources.covers: Egypt, Morocco and South Africa add a 10% service charge to the bill at popular restaurants; if there isn't one, it's common to leave a tip of around 10 to 15%. Read as raw page text.

sources.title: Country-by-country guide: tipping practices across 7 Middle Eastern destinations (Mighty Travels blog, Nov 2024)
sources.covers: Travel blog, used as a second view: many Egyptian restaurants already include a service charge, yet customers are generally still expected to tip separately.

sources.title: Egyptian Tax Authority: VAT Law 67 of 2016
sources.covers: Standard VAT rate 14% from fiscal year 2017/2018.

sources.title: Egyptian Tax Authority: VAT refund for departing visitors
sources.covers: Visitors can refund VAT if stay is 3 months or less and invoices total at least EGP 1,500.

shopTaxes.name: VAT
shopTaxes.basis: standard rate; shelf prices usually include it

rules.shopNote: VAT 14%. Foreign visitors staying up to 3 months can claim VAT back on invoices of at least EGP 1,500.

rules.name: Israel

taxes.name: VAT
taxes.basis: rate since 1 Jan 2025; the Consumer Protection Law requires the displayed price to include VAT

serviceCharge.note: Restaurants almost never add a service charge, except for large groups.

tip.note: Tip 10-12% for good service and 15% for excellent (15% is the norm in Tel Aviv), ideally in cash.

rules.note: No Ministry of Tourism tipping page could be read; the three tipping sources (a hotel-chain blog, a news magazine, a community travel wiki) agree on 10-15%.

sources.title: Consumer Protection Law, 5741-1981, section 17A (Hebrew, Nevo legal database)
sources.covers: 'Total price' means the price including all payments for the item or service and all taxes applicable to it and collected by the dealer. Read as raw page text.

sources.title: Israel: other taxes - PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries (reviewed Jun 2026)
sources.covers: The current rate of VAT is 18%. Professional-services summary, not the tax authority; gov.il returned 403 to scripts.

sources.title: VAT liability for tips - Afik & Co law firm (1 Jan 2025)
sources.covers: An Official Gazette order raised VAT from 17% to 18% on 1 Jan 2025.

sources.title: Tipping in Israel: Who, When, and How Much to Tip (Dan Hotels blog, 28 Aug 2025; a hotel chain)
sources.covers: Restaurants and cafes: 10-12% for good service, 15% for excellent; not usually included in the bill; cash preferred.

sources.title: Who and how to tip on your next trip to Israel (ISRAEL21c, news magazine; undated; read via the Wayback Machine)
sources.covers: The standard restaurant tip used to be 10 percent; it has risen to about 12%, and in Tel Aviv to 15; exceptional service around 20.

sources.title: Israel - Wikivoyage (community travel guide, undated)
sources.covers: The norm for waiters is a 15% tip; where a service charge is included in the bill, don't tip. Community-edited, used only as a third view.

sources.title: Israel Tax Authority: VAT refund for tourists who purchased goods in Israel (updated 17 Feb 2026; read in the in-app browser)
sources.covers: Under Article 43b of the VAT Law a tourist is entitled on departure to a refund of VAT paid on goods bought in a business approved by the Ministry of Tourism.

shopTaxes.name: VAT
shopTaxes.basis: rate since 1 Jan 2025; already included in the shelf price

rules.shopNote: VAT 18% is included in the price. Tourists can claim VAT back on goods bought at approved shops when leaving.

rules.name: Jordan

taxes.name: General sales tax
taxes.basis: added to the restaurant bill (Ministry of Tourism spokesperson); licensed tourist restaurants and hotels were cut to 8% in 2020, 2026 status not confirmed

serviceCharge.note: Many restaurants add a 10% 'service' line; it is a custom, not set by law.

tip.note: Tip about 10% on top of the bill, unless a service charge is already on it.

rules.note: Menu prices usually exclude the 16% sales tax and any 10% service line, so a bill can run up to about a quarter above the menu total.

sources.title: Is the 10% restaurant service tax legal? - Jordan Zad (Arabic; undated)
sources.covers: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities spokesperson: 16% sales tax is added to the restaurant bill; the 10% service charge is a custom among restaurants and no specific law covers it. Read as raw page text.

sources.title: Jordan: other taxes - PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries
sources.covers: General sales tax, similar to VAT, is imposed at 16% on sales of goods and services. The Income and Sales Tax Department site is a script app and could not be read.

sources.title: Sales tax cut for hotels and tourist restaurants to 8% and services to 5% - Ammon News (15 Jun 2020; Arabic headline)
sources.covers: Headline reports sales tax for hotels and tourist restaurants cut to 8% and services to 5%. 2020 measure; whether it still applies in 2026 is unconfirmed.

sources.title: 750 non-tourist restaurants await sales tax reduction: JCC - Jordan News (Oct 2022)
sources.covers: The Chamber of Commerce asked for non-tourist restaurants to be cut from 16 to 8 percent, as tourist restaurants had been.

sources.title: Local Customs (Jordan Tourism Board, undated)
sources.covers: Do tip waiters approximately 10% gratuity in addition to the bill (unless a service charge is included in the total bill). Read as raw page text.

sources.title: The Ultimate Guide to Tipping in the Middle East (Lonely Planet, 27 Sep 2024)
sources.covers: In the UAE, Qatar, Jordan and Saudi Arabia servers expect a 10 to 15% tip at the end of a meal. Read as raw page text.

rules.name: Qatar

serviceCharge.note: Most hospitality outlets include a service charge in the bill.

tip.note: A service charge is usually in the bill; an extra 10-15% in cash is appreciated.

rules.note: Tax inclusion in menu prices was not sourced.

sources.title: Qatar Travel Tips (Visit Qatar, undated)
sources.covers: Most hospitality outlets in Qatar include a service charge in the bill; a tip of 10-15% as a gesture of satisfaction is appreciated; carry cash for tipping. Nothing on taxes.

sources.title: The Ultimate Guide to Tipping in the Middle East (Lonely Planet, Emily Frost, 27 Sep 2024)
sources.covers: UAE, Qatar, Jordan and Saudi Arabia: servers expect a 10-15% tip at the end of a meal; taxis in Jordan round up. Israel and Morocco not covered.

sources.title: Qatar General Tax Authority: Investor's guide
sources.covers: Qatar has not applied the Value Added Tax (VAT).

rules.shopNote: No VAT or general sales tax; the price on the tag is what you pay.

rules.name: Saudi Arabia

taxes.name: VAT
taxes.basis: standard rate; prices must be displayed VAT-inclusive at the point of sale

serviceCharge.note: Restaurants may not add service charges (Ministry of Commerce decision, reconfirmed 2017).

tip.note: Servers generally expect a 10-15% tip at the end of the meal.

rules.note: Tipping is not mandatory and no service charge is added, so a 10-15% tip is not doubled up.

sources.title: ZATCA: Amendments to the Implementing Regulation of VAT, guideline (Issue 1, April 2025)
sources.covers: VAT applies at the standard rate of 15%. Read as raw PDF text; general VAT guideline, not restaurant-specific.

sources.title: Ministry of Commerce: the product price on the shelf includes VAT
sources.covers: The shelf price includes VAT and must match the invoice. Used for the restaurant row's VAT-inclusive pricing; replaces a ZATCA page that no longer loads.

sources.title: Commerce to Al-Eqtisadiah: the decision banning service fees in restaurants continues (Al-Eqtisadiah newspaper, 17 Apr 2017; Arabic headline)
sources.covers: Headline: the Ministry of Commerce says the decision banning service charges in restaurants stays in force and penalties are immediate. 2017; no 2026 reconfirmation found.

sources.title: Saudi tourism: the pros of guided tours - Visit Saudi (official tourism, undated; text sits in the page's embedded data)
sources.covers: In restaurants, tipping is not mandatory but it is recommended to tip between 10 and 15 percent.

sources.title: The Ultimate Guide to Tipping in the Middle East (Lonely Planet, 27 Sep 2024)
sources.covers: In the UAE, Qatar, Jordan and Saudi Arabia servers in restaurants will expect a 10 to 15% tip at the end of a meal. Read as raw page text.

rules.name: Kenya

taxes.name: VAT
taxes.basis: general rate (KRA); whether menu prices include it was not verified

tip.note: Tipping isn't required, but about 10% of the bill for a good meal is appreciated.

rules.note: VAT is 16% and licensed tourism businesses also pay a 2% levy on food and drink sales. No law on menu pricing was found, so check the menu for 'inclusive of VAT'.

sources.title: Kenya Revenue Authority: Value Added Tax
sources.covers: There are two tax rates: 16% (general rate) for all taxable goods and services other than zero-rated supplies, and 0% (zero rate). Read as raw page text; not restaurant-specific.

sources.title: Kenya Law: The Tourism Levy Order (Legal Notice 198 of 2015, consolidated to 31 Dec 2022)
sources.covers: A levy of two per centum of the gross receipts from monthly sales of food, drinks, accommodation and other services applies to the enterprises the notice names. A cost to operators; whether it appears on diners' bills was not verified.

sources.title: 16 things to know before traveling to Kenya (Lonely Planet, 13 Jul 2026)
sources.covers: Tipping isn't expected in Kenya, but for a good meal or service a bonus of around 10% is appreciated.

sources.title: Tipping in Kenya (Expert Africa, a safari tour operator; undated)
sources.covers: A tipping culture has become well established; ten percent of the bill for your waiter would be appropriate. Tour operator, not a tourism board.

sources.title: The Ultimate Guide to Tipping in Africa (Lonely Planet, 27 Sep 2024)
sources.covers: Elsewhere in Africa leaving 10 to 15% is a normal tip for good service in restaurants. Does not name Kenya, so general background only. Read as raw page text.

sources.title: Kenya Revenue Authority: VAT FAQ
sources.covers: 16% applies to taxable goods and services other than zero-rated supplies.

shopTaxes.name: VAT
shopTaxes.basis: general rate; shelf prices normally include it

rules.shopNote: VAT 16% on most goods (8% on petroleum).

rules.name: Tanzania

taxes.name: VAT
taxes.basis: mainland rate; prices advertised by registered businesses must include it (VAT Act s.38)

tip.note: About 10% is customary at restaurants, up to 15% for very good service; always in cash.

rules.note: Prices advertised by VAT-registered businesses must include 18% VAT. No Tanzania Tourist Board tipping page could be read; the tipping sources are safari operators and Lonely Planet's Africa guide.

sources.title: Tanzania Revenue Authority: The Value Added Tax Act (Cap. 148, copy on TRA site)
sources.covers: Section 38(1): a price advertised or quoted by a registered person for a taxable supply shall be value added tax inclusive. Read as raw PDF text.

sources.title: Tanzania Revenue Authority: Taxes and duties at a glance 2025/2026 (read via the Wayback Machine)
sources.covers: VAT on taxable goods and services in Mainland Tanzania: 18%.

sources.title: Tanzania money, budget and tipping (Tanzania Experience, a safari operator; (c) 2026)
sources.covers: At restaurants, a tip of 10% is customary; always tip in cash. Tour operator.

sources.title: The Ultimate Guide to Tipping in Africa (Lonely Planet, 27 Sep 2024)
sources.covers: Elsewhere in Africa leaving 10 to 15% is a normal tip for good service in restaurants; Tanzania is named in the page's country list but not given its own restaurant figure. Read as raw page text.

rules.shopNote: VAT 18% is included in the price (advertised prices of VAT-registered sellers must include VAT).
